toolCalls.name: StructuredOutput

output.brief:
The departures are concentrated in one place. Eight of the 11 associates on Kestrel have resigned, against 1 of the 13 who never worked on it. That points away from firm-wide pay, the firm-wide hours target and general market movement. None of those would hit one team so unevenly. The £12k payment would likely miss the cause, so don't announce it or close the review.

What I can't tell yet is whether the cause is Kestrel's workload or Dorian Faulk's supervision. All 11 Kestrel associates worked only under Faulk, and Faulk supervised nothing else. Kestrel hours were about 2,270 a year, with weekend work on 31% of weekends. That is well above the rest of the group. Associates also described late-night drafts with corrections copied to the whole team. Faulk himself told Priya Lindqvist in March that he was keeping people late and that the team was stretched. The records can't separate the two explanations, and I'm moderately sure of that.

Next steps: commission the external confidential interviews (about £9k), designed to separate supervision from workload. Four leavers have already agreed to take part. Meanwhile, consider low-cost interim steps such as monitoring weekend work. Hold the contract-reviewer spend (£160k) and the change of supervisor until the interviews are done. Add matter and supervising-partner fields to attrition reporting.
